questions.q: What does a Salesforce administrator primarily do, according to this lesson?
options: Writes all of the Salesforce Platform's underlying source code
Configures and maintains a Salesforce org day to day, mostly using point-and-click tools without writing code
Only sells AppExchange listings to new customers
Designs enterprise-wide architecture for multiple connected orgs
questions.explain: The administrator customizes pre-built applications and manages users, security, and automation, mostly without code.

questions.q: How does this lesson distinguish a developer's work from an administrator's?
options: A developer only fixes bugs reported by administrators
There is no real difference between the two roles
A developer exclusively manages user permissions and security settings
A developer builds custom logic, integrations, and new applications on the platform, while an admin customizes what's already there
questions.explain: Where an admin customizes existing, pre-built applications, a developer builds genuinely new things directly on the platform.

questions.q: Where does this lesson say a consultant typically works?
options: Exclusively inside Salesforce's own corporate headquarters
Only as a freelance AppExchange app reviewer
Usually for a partner firm, helping a client figure out what to build before configuration or code happens
Always as a direct employee of the client company, never a partner firm
questions.explain: Consultants typically work at partner firms (connecting back to Lesson 9's ecosystem), gathering requirements and managing implementations for client businesses.

questions.q: What does an architect do, according to this lesson?
options: Only handles entry-level data entry tasks
Exclusively writes marketing copy for AppExchange listings
Replaces the need for administrators entirely
Designs how a large, complex Salesforce implementation fits together — data model, security, integrations, and performance
questions.explain: The architect is the most senior, most technical role, focused on how a complex implementation fits together as a whole.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe the relationship between the four roles?
options: Each role works in total isolation and never interacts with the others
Only one of the four roles is ever needed on any given project
They're different altitudes on the same ecosystem, not competing titles — a typical implementation touches all four
Administrators always outrank and directly supervise architects
questions.explain: A typical implementation involves a consultant scoping it, an architect designing it, a developer building custom pieces, and an admin maintaining it afterward.
